design_parameters.title: Electrode design — BatPaC-style (NMC111)
design_parameters.description: Set the electrode design; material and process quantities for 1 kg of cell, and the cell's Wh/kg, follow from it.

derived.electrolyte_g_cm2: (t_pos_cm * porosity + t_neg_cm * porosity + separator_um * 1e-4 * separator_porosity) * rho_electrolyte
derived.unit_g_cm2: coat_pos_g_cm2 + coat_neg_g_cm2 + al_g_cm2 + cu_g_cm2 + sep_g_cm2 + electrolyte_g_cm2

notes: Equations: BatPaC v5.0 manual (Knehr et al., Argonne ANL/CSE-22/1, 2022), §5.2 — capacity = Q·ρ·ε·A·δ (Eq. 5.2), negative sized from the N/P ratio (§5.2.3), bi-cell layer of foils, coatings and separators (Eq. 5.33).
Slider defaults from the manual (Table 3.1, energy couple): porosity 0.35, Al 15 µm, Cu 10 µm, cathode 96:2:2, graphite 98:0:2, N/P 1.1.

Not in the manual (BatPaC keeps these in its Chem sheet): specific capacities, material densities, average voltage, separator porosity and density, electrolyte density, separator and cathode thickness defaults. Literature-typical values; replace with BatPaC's.

Simplified: thickness is an input, so BatPaC's power/impedance solver is not run. Electrode overhang, uncoated foil tabs and the C/3 voltage loss are ignored; tabs and pouch stay at the template's ecoinvent masses. The Wh/kg is therefore an upper bound for a finished cell.
Process energy and solvent use scale per kg of component, as in the ecoinvent data. Before Apply, the inventory holds ecoinvent's own cell composition.
